Continuation of the Same Subject.</title> <div sID="gen19877" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11034"/><hi type="bold">2. mountains of Israel--</hi>that is, of Palestine in general. The mountains are addressed by personification; implying that the Israelites themselves are incurable and unworthy of any more appeals; so the prophet sent to Jeroboam did not deign to address the king, but addressed the altar (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.13.2">1Ki 13:2</reference>). The mountains are specified as being the scene of Jewish idolatries on "the high places" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.6.3">Eze 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.26.30">Le 26:30</reference>). <div eID="gen19877" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11041"/><div sID="gen19885" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11041"/><hi type="bold">9. they that escape of you shall remember me--</hi>The object of God's chastisements shall at last be effected by working in them true contrition. This partially took place in the complete eradication of idolatry from the Jews ever since the Babylonian captivity. But they have yet to repent of their crowning sin, the crucifixion of Messiah; their full repentance is therefore future, after the ordeal of trials for many centuries, ending with that foretold in <reference osisRef="Zech.10.9">Zec 10:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.13.8">13:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.13.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.1-Zech.14.4">14:1-4</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.14.11">11</reference>. "They shall remember me in far countries" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.7.16">Eze 7:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.30.1-Deut.30.8">De 30:1-8</reference>).<div eID="gen19885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19886" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I am broken with their whorish heart--</hi>Fairbairn translates, actively, "I will break" their whorish heart; English Version is better. In their exile they shall remember how long I bore with them, but was at last compelled to punish, after I was "broken" (My long-suffering wearied out) by their desperate (<reference osisRef="Num.15.39">Nu 15:39</reference>) spiritual whorishness [Calvin], (<reference osisRef="Ps.78.40">Psa 78:40</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.7.13">Is 7:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.43.24">43:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.63.10">63:10</reference>).<div eID="gen19886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19887" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">loathe themselves--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Lev.26.39-Lev.26.45">Le 26:39-45</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.42.6">Job 42:6</reference>). They shall not wait for men to condemn them but shall condemn themselves (<reference osisRef="Ezek.20.43">Eze 20:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.31">36:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.42.6">Job 42:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.11.31">1Co 11:31</reference>). <div eID="gen19887" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 9. they that escape of you shall remember me-- The object of God's chastisements shall at last be effected by working in them true contrition. This partially took place in the complete eradication of idolatry from the Jews ever since the Babylonian captivity. But they have yet to repent of their crowning sin, the crucifixion of Messiah; their full repentance is therefore future, after the ordeal of trials for many centuries, ending with that foretold in Zec 10:9 ; 13:8 , 9 ; 14:1-4 , 11 . "They shall remember me in far countries" ( Eze 7:16 ; De 30:1-8 ). I am broken with their whorish heart-- Fairbairn translates, actively, "I will break" their whorish heart; English Version is better. In their exile they shall remember how long I bore with them, but was at last compelled to punish, after I was "broken" (My long-suffering wearied out) by their desperate ( Nu 15:39 ) spiritual whorishness [Calvin], ( Psa 78:40 ; Is 7:13 ; 43:24 ; 63:10 ). loathe themselves-- ( Le 26:39-45 ; Job 42:6 ). They shall not wait for men to condemn them but shall condemn themselves ( Eze 20:43 ; 36:31 ; Job 42:6 ; 1Co 11:31 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11042"/><div sID="gen19888" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11042"/>11. Gesticulations vividly setting before the hearers the greatness of the calamity about to be inflicted. In indignation at the abominations of Israel extend thine hand towards Judea, as if about to "strike," and "stamp," shaking off the dust with thy foot, in token of how God shall "stretch out His hand upon them," and tread them down (<reference osisRef="Ezek.6.14">Eze 6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.14">Eze 21:14</reference>). <div eID="gen19888" type="x-p"/>
